query: Which imaging modality and immobilization strategy (light-sheet, two-photon, confocal; agarose, microfluidic trap, anesthetic) will permit reliable co-registration of tp53/H2AX reporters with pan-neuronal GCaMP during sleep and wake, and what spatial/temporal resolution is minimally required?

response.query: Which imaging modality and immobilization strategy (light-sheet, two-photon, confocal; agarose, microfluidic trap, anesthetic) will permit reliable co-registration of tp53/H2AX reporters with pan-neuronal GCaMP during sleep and wake, and what spatial/temporal resolution is minimally required?
response.answer: Two-photon microscopy with agarose immobilization allows reliable co-registration of tp53/H2AX reporters with pan-neuronal GCaMP during sleep and wake, with spatial resolution of ~1 µm and temporal resolution of ~30 ms.
